issue_plan.name: Attribute independent component evidence
issue_plan.summary: Three ordered changes add trusted assumptions, conformance observations, and runtime tests and assertions alongside exact-target proof evidence, using only caller-supplied records. Each change preserves other evidence kinds through atomic replacement, validates retained provenance, and binds the resulting report in canonical JSON and fingerprints without running checks or changing the gate outcome. Each updates SPEC.md and README.md for the APIs it ships, including the limited Markdown view and the continued execution restriction. The merger must record the new evidence and assumption policy; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Preserve independent component evidence and attribute declared assumptions
issues.body:
Build the first part of #270 on #257's merged declaration/input foundation. internal/project already resolves assumptions, selected checks, inert invocations and separate test/driver/input snapshots. Add supplied trusted-assumption records to internal/verify's API and JSON, making proof and assumption attribution independent, atomic replacements. Attribute caller-supplied facts only; add no execution, instrumentation, discovery or gate connection.

Keep AttributeComponentProofs and the existing ComponentProofResult fields and proof-row JSON contract. A target is proved only when its own supplied result passed, names a verifier, has no errors, explicitly verifies that exact canonical target, covers every selected contract and supplies matching source/contract snapshots for every verified and checked-contract declaration. Missing or incomplete proof remains unchecked. Helpers, selected contracts, same-named functions and neighbors inherit no proof, even when named in another target's verified list. Preserve valid existing proof callers whose results include additional known verified declarations, checked contracts beyond the selection, or additional matching input snapshots: validate those references without requiring equality to the selected sets, and confer coverage only on the result's target.

Add optional actual proof invocation/input provenance without newly requiring it for a previously valid proof-only call. When supplied, it must match its selected proof invocation by target, kind, canonical check ID and invocation ID, including command, ordered arguments, working directory, explicit environment and sampling values. Validate all supplied actual file snapshots against the declaration/input provenance; bind the selected source and every additional supplied execution input, including non-Go data and model/dependency files. Retain and fingerprint supplied tool identity/pins and actual invocation metadata. Keep declaration snapshots in the existing proof Inputs field; do not replace that compatibility contract with file-only inputs. Missing optional metadata in old calls must not weaken existing proof rules or synthesize an invocation.

Add an attribution operation for explicitly supplied assumptions. Each record names an exact configured production target and one of that target's declared assumption IDs, retaining the target's source/contract snapshot and the declaration's identity, statement, reason/origin and source path/hash. Require an exact match to that selected declaration; unknown, duplicate, unselected or stale records are errors. Label records assumed/unverified in the API and JSON. An assumption is a declaration, never a tool result: it cannot prove a component, pass a runtime or conformance check, satisfy missing proof contracts or attempts, or change gate pass/fail. An inventory assumption without a supplied record remains inventory data, not recorded evidence.

Refactor internal/verify/components.go and verify.go so each operation validates a detached candidate before committing, replacing or clearing only its own kind. Reject invalid batches atomically, including a bad record after valid ones: serialized report JSON and its stored and recomputed fingerprints must remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Replacing the inventory also revalidates every retained kind against its declarations, selections and snapshots, rejecting stale or unselected retained evidence instead of discarding it or silently changing its coverage. Apply this on clears too. Canonically equivalent reordered inventories remain valid. Apply this to proof and assumptions now; later kinds extend the same rule.

Use canonical component/check IDs, not bare names; assumption IDs remain target-local, and invocation IDs local to (target, kind, check). Validate references using production components for targets and the foundation's separate provenance for selected checks and files, without adding test/driver-only declarations as production rows. Reject unknown or duplicate references and mismatched source/contract/file snapshots, including invalid replacement inventories. The report must own deep copies of every nested collection, including invocation maps, arguments and file lists. Recompute the fingerprint once on success; preserve legacy checks, gate pass/fail, ratified data and model-only restrictions.

JSON retains complete production inventory, compatible sorted proof rows for every component including unchecked ones, and independent assumption records. A component can carry proof and assumptions simultaneously; an assumed neighbor remains unproved. CodeAssurance and Claim remain component evidence and EverySize remains false, including decoded reports with a stale assurance label. No score or aggregate proof label merges kinds. Fingerprint's canonical copying, including after JSON decoding, binds assumption contents/source, declarations/selections, optional proof provenance, all inputs and tool pins. Preserve set/completion-order and relocation stability, meaningful argument order and existing volatile exclusions; legacy reports retain their successful JSON, fingerprints and rendering.

Acceptance uses supplied records only. Test proof plus assumptions on one target, an assumed-only neighbor, and a proof-contract helper that never inherits proof; absent assumption records must not be invented. Cover old proof calls without invocation metadata and valid extra known verified/contract/input references, as well as incomplete/failed proof. Exercise unknown, duplicate, bare-name, unselected, stale and late-batch failures, checking byte-for-byte rollback. Replace and clear proof and assumptions in both orders under both gate outcomes, preserving legacy checks and ratified data. Replacing assumptions must reject retained stale target/contract/proof-input or invocation snapshots; replacing proof must reject a retained changed/removed assumption, including text, reason, target or source. Test reordered equivalent inventories, relocation, every new semantic fingerprint input and caller mutation of all nested input collections. Retain existing proof, provenance and legacy compatibility tests. Sentinel commands must confirm no attribution execution and verify.ErrComponents before explicit code verification starts tools. Model-only checking stays available; model-only reports reject attribution.

Update SPEC.md and README.md in this change for the actual APIs, JSON, proof compatibility, assumption labeling, replacement/staleness semantics, fingerprint inputs and execution limits. Correct Report documentation and explicit receipt/footer tool-output-only claims to allow declared assumptions and supplied data. State that Markdown currently shows component proof coverage; new evidence details remain in JSON until the separate presentation work outside #270. Preserve all legacy Markdown and the existing literal-escaping protections. Update the old explicit-footer delimiter assertion in internal/receipt/explicit_literals_accept_test.go while retaining its escaping/structure assertions and legacy goldens. Do not edit pinned statements or ratified locks.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161, D-0163, D-0168, D-0122 and D-0105. Cite supporting decisions on changed SPEC bullets. The merger records the new attribution, replacement and trusted-assumption policy; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Attribute supplied component conformance and attempt coverage
issues.body:
Build #270's second part on the merged proof/assumption attribution API. Add independent supplied conformance records to internal/verify's API and JSON, using #257's selected driver and invocation/input provenance apart from production coverage. Run no driver, model checker, adapter or other tool; infer no evidence from source or legacy checks and connect no gate path.

Each record names the exact configured production target, canonical selected conformance driver/check, selected invocation identity, runner/tool identity and pins, actual outcome and diagnostics. Retain matching target/contract and driver snapshots, reproducible invocation metadata (command, ordered arguments, working directory, explicit environment and sampling values), all actual execution inputs, model identity, ratified bounds, sampled or bounded-exhaustive mode, observed run/step/state/transition counts, model state count and distinct attempt-coverage information. Multiple selected checks/invocations must remain distinguishable. A selected driver outside production scope contributes provenance only; it must not add production coverage rows.

Require executable records to reference their selected conformance check and invocation, with matching declaration and input snapshots. Actual inputs include the selected source and every additional file supplied to the run, including non-Go fixtures, configuration, dependency manifests/lockfiles, model sources/includes and the ratified-bounds source. Bind the supplied model identity to its exact model/input snapshots and the supplied ratified bounds to their source snapshots and applicable report bounds. Inventory stores these files as declared inputs; Design.Spec is not model-source identity. Document matching without parsing/discovering omitted files, changing ratification or inferring this execution from legacy checks.

Keep the actual supplied mode and outcome even when a coverage claim must be qualified. Successful sampled observations never imply exhaustive coverage. An exhaustive-state claim requires supplied bounded-exhaustive mode, successful nonempty conformance, positive matching observed/model state counts and no failed attempt check, following D-0161. Missing attempt coverage is not checked; only successful nonempty attempt-coverage evidence establishes every step tried. A present unsuccessful attempt check also blocks exhaustive-state coverage; failed, timed-out, skipped or empty attempt coverage establishes no every-step claim. Preserve successful checked-transition evidence separately from an unsuccessful attempt-coverage check. Absent attempt coverage alone must not prevent D-0161's state-coverage claim.

Declarations, positive counts and a successful process/package result cannot replace actual conformance outcomes. Missing runner identity, missing required execution inputs, no actually exercised checks, failed, timed-out, skipped, empty or missing conformance outcomes must never yield successful evidence. Well-formed unsuccessful or incomplete attempts may remain visible with diagnostics; supplied stale, unknown, duplicate or unselected references are attribution errors. No absent result may be synthesized as a successful run, and conformance never grants proof to the target, its helper, driver or neighbor.

Use detached validation before commit. Replacing/clearing conformance preserves proof, assumptions, legacy checks, gate pass/fail and ratified data. On replacement inventory, proof/assumption operations revalidate retained conformance, and conformance operations revalidate retained proof/assumptions. Reject atomically when any retained evidence would become stale or unselected. In particular, an outside-scope driver-only edit must invalidate retained conformance during a proof update, even when every production source is unchanged. Model/include/ratified-lock inputs, bounds, invocation, selected driver, target/contract or any other referenced input changes cannot be hidden by updating another kind. Reordered but canonically equivalent inventories remain valid.

Extend JSON with independent conformance/attempt evidence, preserving complete production inventory and proof rows/statuses. A conformance-only neighbor stays unproved; proof, assumptions and conformance can coexist without a score or aggregate proof claim. CodeAssurance and Claim remain component evidence and EverySize remains false. Deep-copy all nested record values, model/bounds maps, invocation values, input snapshots, observations, attempt information and diagnostics. Canonicalize sets and result completion order both for storage and Fingerprint, including decoded reports, without reordering meaningful argument or observation sequences. Bind every new semantic value, outcome, count, mode, input hash and tool pin; preserve relocation stability, volatile exclusions and successful legacy JSON/fingerprints/rendering. Recompute the fingerprint once after successful validation.

Acceptance uses supplied records only. Exercise sampled and bounded-exhaustive conformance, each with absent, failed, empty and successful attempt coverage; positive equal state counts, mismatches and zero counts; and successful transitions surviving failed attempt coverage. Exercise failed, timed-out, skipped, empty, absent and incomplete conformance, including missing identity/input/outcome with positive counts. Test exact selected canonical drivers, multiple checks/invocations, out-of-scope drivers and a conformance-only production neighbor and helper that remain unproved. Unknown, duplicate, bare-name, unselected, stale and late-batch failures must preserve serialized JSON and stored/recomputed fingerprints byte-for-byte.

Test proof, assumptions and conformance attribution/update/clear in different orders under both gate outcomes, retaining legacy checks and ratified data. Cross-kind replacement failures must cover both directions: retained conformance invalidated by outside-scope driver edits, target/contract edits, invocation edits, non-Go data/dependency/model/include/ratified-lock edits or bounds changes while updating proof/assumptions; and retained proof or assumptions invalidated while updating conformance. Check equivalent reordered inventories, relocation, each new fingerprint input/outcome, and caller mutation of nested collections. Keep old proof callers valid without new invocation metadata and with additional known verified declarations, checked contracts or matching snapshots. Sentinels must confirm no attribution execution and verify.ErrComponents before verify.Check/Run start tools. Model-only checking stays available; model-only reports reject attribution.

Update SPEC.md and README.md for the shipped conformance API and JSON, success/exhaustive/attempt distinctions, matching model/bounds and execution-input provenance, replacement/staleness semantics and fingerprint inputs. Describe Markdown's limited proof view and JSON's new details. Keep Report/explicit receipt language compatible with assumptions and legacy rendering unchanged. Explicit component code verification remains unavailable; do not edit pinned statements or ratified locks.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0082, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161, D-0163, D-0168, D-0122 and the preceding issue's recorded attribution/assumption policy. Cite supporting decisions on changed SPEC bullets. The merger records new conformance attribution policy; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.

issues.title: Attribute runtime tests and assertions alongside other component evidence
issues.body:
Complete #270 on the merged proof/assumption and conformance APIs. Add supplied runtime-check records to internal/verify's API/JSON and acceptance of all four kinds together, using the separate selected-test and invocation provenance. Add no assertion discovery, production instrumentation, execution protocol, adapter, tool execution or gate connection.

Runtime records name the exact configured production target, canonical selected tests/checks, selected invocation identity, runner/tool identity and pins, actual per-test outcomes, the assertions actually exercised with their identities and per-assertion outcomes, and diagnostics. Retain matching target/contract and test/check snapshots, reproducible invocation metadata and every actual execution input supplied by the caller. Match the selected invocation's command, ordered arguments, working directory, explicit environment/sampling data and declared input snapshots. Include the selected source and every additional supplied file, including non-Go fixtures/configuration and dependency/model inputs. Report assertions only from supplied exercised outcomes tied to their selected test/snapshots; require no assertion discovery.

A successful process/package test, a configured test name or a legacy build result cannot imply that any target or assertion was exercised. A target association says which check was selected, not that the target's code was covered. Report only actually supplied tests/assertions and their outcomes; never fill unreported selections with successful results. Missing runner identity, required inputs or an actual exercised outcome, and failed, timed-out, skipped or empty outcomes, cannot yield success for that test/assertion. A supplied passing test can stand without assertion records, but cannot manufacture them. Counts and declarations do not substitute for outcomes. Preserve well-formed unsuccessful/incomplete records with diagnostics without upgrading failed or unexercised assertions. Runtime evidence cannot establish proof, exhaustive conformance, every-step coverage or assumption validation.

New records must reference their target's selected tests/checks and invocation using canonical component IDs, with matching source/contract and input snapshots. Reject unknown, duplicate, bare-name, unselected and stale references atomically, including duplicates within nested test/assertion/input collections and invalid records after valid ones. Retain distinct selected checks/invocations while rejecting duplicates. Keep the earlier proof allowance for additional known verified declarations, checked contracts and input snapshots; do not apply new-kind selection restrictions to valid old proof results.

Validate a detached candidate before committing, replacing/clearing only runtime evidence. Preserve proof, conformance, assumptions, legacy checks, gate pass/fail, ratified data and model-only restrictions. Every operation, including clears, revalidates retained kinds against replacement inventory and applicable model/bounds context. Rejection leaves serialized report JSON and stored/recomputed fingerprints byte-for-byte unchanged. In particular, proof or runtime updates with an outside-scope driver-only edit must reject stale retained conformance; conformance/assumption updates must reject retained runtime evidence after test/input or invocation edits. Target/contract, selection, assumption content/source, model/include/ratified-bounds or any referenced execution input change must not be hidden by an update to another kind. Accept canonically equivalent reordered inventories.

JSON keeps complete production inventory including unchecked neighbors and files without functions, compatible proof rows/statuses, and independent conformance, runtime and assumption records. A target may have all four kinds at once. A conformance-only neighbor and a helper named as a proof contract or verified declaration stay unproved without their own qualifying target proof; assumed-only components remain unverified. CodeAssurance and Claim remain component evidence and EverySize remains false, including after decoding stale assurance labels. Do not add scores or an aggregate proof label.

The report owns deep copies of all nested runtime collections and all retained kinds. Canonical fingerprints bind declaration/selection identities, assumption contents/source, actual invocations and all supplied input hashes, model/bounds, outcomes, observations, attempt coverage and tool pins. Include runtime test/assertion identities, actual per-item outcomes and diagnostics. Preserve set/result-completion-order and relocation stability while retaining meaningful invocation argument and observation order. Preserve existing volatile exclusions and legacy successful fingerprints, JSON and Markdown. Canonicalize in Fingerprint on decoded reports as well as attribution; recompute once per successful update.

Acceptance must include a target with proof, conformance, runtime assertions and assumptions simultaneously; a conformance-only neighbor; an assumed-only neighbor; and a selected proof-contract helper with no proof of its own. Runtime cases include multiple selected tests/invocations with actual passing/failing assertions, a package/process pass with no actual test/assertion evidence, configured but unreported tests, and failed, timed-out, skipped, empty, missing and incomplete attempts. Exercise unknown/duplicate/unselected/stale IDs and snapshots, and valid records followed by invalid ones, requiring byte-for-byte rollback.

Complete the cross-kind matrix through public APIs: attribute/update/clear each kind in different orders, preserve every other kind under both gate outcomes, preserve legacy checks and ratified data, and permit canonically equivalent reordered replacement inventories. Test retained staleness in both directions for target/source and contract changes; test-source, fixture/configuration/dependency inputs and invocation changes; assumption identity/text/reason/source changes; and model/include/ratified-lock/bounds changes. Specifically edit only an outside-scope driver, then try both a proof update and a runtime update while retaining conformance. Verify every new semantic input/outcome changes fingerprints while set/completion order and relocation do not, meaningful argument order does, and caller mutation of all nested supplied values cannot mutate stored evidence. Include JSON round trips with all four kinds.

Retain all earlier proof, provenance, conformance, assumption and legacy compatibility tests, including proof-only calls without invocation metadata, valid extra known verified/checked-contract/input declarations and incomplete proofs that remain unchecked. Reexercise sampled/bounded-exhaustive observations with missing/failed/successful attempt coverage, preserving successful transitions independently. Sentinels must confirm no attribution execution and verify.ErrComponents before explicit code verification starts tools. Model-only checking stays available; model-only reports reject attribution. Complete #270's API and validation coverage here.

Update SPEC.md and README.md for all four APIs/JSON, runtime/assertion success, replacement/staleness, fingerprints and execution limits. Retain accurate Report documentation and explicit receipt/footer language allowing declared assumptions. State that Markdown displays component proof coverage while JSON holds the new details until the separate presentation change. Preserve legacy rendering and literal escaping. Do not edit ratified statements or locks.

Decisions: D-0013, D-0024, D-0029, D-0082, D-0135, D-0152, D-0158, D-0161, D-0163, D-0168, D-0122 and the evidence/assumption policies recorded as preceding issues merge. Cite supporting decisions on changed SPEC bullets. The merger records new runtime attribution policy; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/.
